For the diagram depicted above, which number corresponds to the point $S$ if $M$ is the midpoint of the line segment $\overset{―}{RS}?$
question.worked_solution:
The point $R$ corresponds to the number ${x}_{1}=-8$ while the midpoint $M$ corresponds to ${x}_{m}=-5.$

To find the number ${x}_{2}$ corresponding to the point $S$, we first set up an equation using the midpoint formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{m} & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\ -5 & =\frac{-8+{x}_{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${x}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-5 & =\frac{-8+{x}_{2}}{2} \\ 2\cdot (-5) & =-8+{x}_{2} \\ -10 & =-8+{x}_{2} \\ -2 & ={x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point $S$ corresponds to ${x}_{2}=-2.$
